links.outcome: Discrimination of PIPRA delirium model on local ICU historical data without recalibration
links.effect: AUROC 0.60 (95% CI 0.49-0.71) among 146 patients, 38 (26%) with delirium; limited discriminative ability; risk overestimation in higher-risk individuals.
links.quote: Pre-Interventional Predictive Risk Assessment yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.60 (95% confidence interval, 0.49-0.71), indicating limited discriminative ability.

links.outcome: Transportability of preoperative delirium model to a different setting (postoperative ICU)
links.effect: Direct application without recalibration showed limited transportability; AUROC 0.60; overestimated risk among higher-risk patients.
links.quote: In this postoperative intensive care unit cohort, direct application of a preoperative delirium prediction model showed limited transportability without recalibration.

links.outcome: Calibration of unmodified model in new local population
links.effect: Reasonable alignment at lower predicted risks but overestimation among higher-risk individuals when applied without recalibration or modification.
links.quote: Calibration analysis suggested reasonable alignment at lower predicted risks, with risk overestimation observed among higher-risk individuals.

screen.reason: The study conducts an external validation of an existing commercial/pre-built clinical predictive risk tool (PIPRA) in a new clinical context (Japanese ICU cohort) to test its transportability without recalibration.
